title: A SIGINT that lands during a boundary refresh is lost: the refresh re-execs and the new process dispatches another wave
summary: At the wave-29 close (2026-09-28 ~23:40) the operator sent SIGINT to the loop while prepareIteration was in its boundary work. The boundary refresh was already rebuilding; it finished, re-pinned (9a1a292e -> a2a1fdb7) and re-execed the same argv. The interrupt had cancelled the old image's context, and exec discarded it, so the new process booted as a fresh run and would have dispatched another wave; a second SIGINT stopped it before cycle 1. Refresher.Refresh never consults the batch context: guards() checks lanes, the breaker and the build commit, but not an interrupt.
fix: The refresh takes the batch context: a cancelled context skips the rebuild and the re-exec (a `skip{"interrupted"}` degrade), and prepareIteration re-checks ctx.Err() after the refresh returns false, so an interrupt that arrives during the rebuild ends the run with stop_reason signal instead of re-execing.
acceptance: A refresh whose context is cancelled before the re-exec does not call ReExec and reports refreshed=false (red today: it re-execs)
prepareIteration returns the interrupt decision when the context is cancelled during the refresh
A refresh with a live context still rebuilds and re-execs as before
source: console, 2026-09-28, wave-29 boundary stop (the loop needed two SIGINTs)
